the Na1 +3 xAl xHf 2− xSi 2 xP 3−2 xO 12 (x ≤ 0.8) system was successfully synthesized from the pyrophyllite starting material.
Na1 + 2.4xAlxHfxSi2 − xP3 − 1.2xO12 is a new Na super ionic conductor (NASICON) material, which possesses a high ionic conductivity of about 0.5 S · cm− 1 at 350°C.
Na1 + 2xAlxHfxSi2 − 2xP3O12 solid electrolytes were prepared in the temperature range of 900–11500 °C, with the highest conductivity of 1.22 mS · cm−1, which was found at x = 0,6 and 350 °C.

synthesis and characterization of new fast sodium conductors based on pyrophyllite, which can be used in sodium batteries.
the synthesis and characterization of the Na1 + xAlxHf1 − xSi2P3 − 3xO12 system, which is a promising candidate for solid-state sodium-ion batteries.
synthesis of Na1 + 2xAlxSi4 − 2xP3O12 (x = 0, 0.1, 0.2) solid solutions, their characterization and evaluation of their ionic conductivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Na1 + xAlxHf3 − xSi2 − xP3 − 3xO12 (x = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6) system represents a new family of sodium superionic conductors, which can be used as solid electrolytes for solid state electrochemical devices.

the Na1 + xAlxHf1 − xSi2P3 − 3xO12 system is the most promising one for the synthesis of fast ion conductors with the highest values of ionic conductivity in the Na1+xAlxHf 1−xSi2P3−3xO12 (0.2 ≤ x ≤ 0) system.
the synthesis of the NASICON structure is possible at a lower temperature (900 °C) with a lower reaction time (2 h) than the reported literature.

the ionic conductivity increases with the increase of the x value, which is due to the increase in the number of the Na+ ions.
the Na1 + xAlxHf 2 − xSi 2xP 3 − 2 xO12 system with x ≤ 0. 6 is a promising candidate for the application in sodium-ion batteries.
the synthesis of the NASICON phase in the system Na1 + 2xAlxHfxSi3 − 2xF2 − xO12 is a promising way for preparing new fast ion conductors with improved properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to prepare NASICON materials in a single-step reaction at relatively low temperature (900 °C) using a natural layered aluminosilosicate as a starting material, which is an important step towards the industrial application of NASICON materials.
the Na1 + xAl2 − xSi3 − 2P3O12 system is a promising material for sodium fast ion conductivities.
the Na1 + xAlxHf 2− xSi2xO12 (0.4 ≤ x ≤ 0 ≤ 0.8) compounds can be synthesized by solid-state synthesis at temperatures lower than those used to prepare the Na3AlHf2Si2P3O12 compound.
